# Architecture diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-architecture/grammar/architecture.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Architecture diagram syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `architecture-beta`
diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed architecture diagrams with Langium (`architecture.langium`,
`arch.langium` and `common.langium` in `@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token
rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords and sides are case-sensitive.

A word keyword gives way to a longer id (`services`, `rows` and `inx` are ids), but a side does
not: `L`, `R`, `T` and `B` are read before an id, so no id can start with one of those capitals
(`Backend` is the side `B` and the id `ackend`). An id that starts with `title` splits too.
Each statement ends its line, except that `architecture-beta` may share its line with the
first one.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A diagram is `architecture-beta`, then statements, each on a line of its own (the first may
share the header's line). The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and `COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are skipped
before parsing.

```ebnf
architecture = { NEWLINE } Header { NEWLINE | statement NEWLINE } [ statement ] EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = ARCHITECTURE_BETA ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Group
          | Service
          | Junction
          | Edge
          | Alignment
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr ;
```

`group id(icon)[Label] in parent`: a group, drawn as a dashed box around what is in it, with
an optional icon and label. A parent group is declared before the group.

```ebnf
Group @Group = GROUP ID [ ICON ] [ LABEL ] [ IN ID ] ;
```

`service id(icon)[Label] in group`: a service, drawn as its icon with the label below; a
text icon in quotes (`service id "text"[Label]`) draws the text in place of an icon.

```ebnf
Service @Service = SERVICE ID [ STRING | ICON ] [ LABEL ] [ IN ID ] ;
```

`junction id in group`: a point where edges meet, drawn as nothing, optionally in a
group.

```ebnf
Junction @Junction = JUNCTION ID [ IN ID ] ;
```

`a:R --> L:b`: an edge from the right side of `a` to the left side of `b`, with optional
arrowheads (`<`, `>`), a label (`-[label]-`) and `{group}` after either id.

```ebnf
Edge @Edge = ID [ ARROW_GROUP ] COLON DIRECTION [ ARROW_INTO ] ( DASH_DASH | DASH LABEL DASH ) [ ARROW_INTO ] DIRECTION COLON ID [ ARROW_GROUP ] ;
```

`align row a b` or `align column a b c`: lines up at least two services or junctions in a
row or a column.

```ebnf
Alignment @Alignment = ALIGN ( ROW | COLUMN ) ID ID { ID } ;
```

`title Shop`: the title, kept for accessibility tools but not drawn (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | ARCHITECTURE_BETA | `architecture-beta(?!-*\w)` |  | `architecture-beta`: starts an architecture diagram. |
| INITIAL | JUNCTION | `junction(?!-*\w)` |  | `junction j in g`: a point where edges meet, drawn as nothing, optionally in a group. |
| INITIAL | SERVICE | `service(?!-*\w)` |  | `service db(database)[Database] in g`: a service with an optional icon (or a text icon in quotes), an optional label in brackets, and an optional group. |
| INITIAL | COLUMN | `column(?!-*\w)` |  | `align column a b`: the members share a column. |
| INITIAL | GROUP | `group(?!-*\w)` |  | `group g(cloud)[Cloud] in parent`: a group with an optional icon, label and parent group. |
| INITIAL | ALIGN | `align(?!-*\w)` |  | `align row a b c`: lines services and junctions up in a row (`row`) or a column (`column`). |
| INITIAL | ROW | `row(?!-*\w)` |  | `align row a b`: the members share a row. |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. It wins over `--` and `-`. |
| INITIAL | DASH_DASH | `--` |  | `--`: an edge without a label, `a:R -- L:b`. |
| INITIAL | IN | `in(?!-*\w)` |  | `in g`: places a service, junction or group in the group `g`, declared before it when it is a group. |
| INITIAL | COLON | `:` |  | `:` between an id and its side: `a:R`, `L:b`. |
| INITIAL | DASH | `-` |  | `-[label]-`: the two dashes around an edge's label. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTION | `[LRTB]` |  | `L`, `R`, `T` or `B`: the side of a service or junction an edge meets (left, right, top, bottom). |
| INITIAL | ARROW_GROUP | `\{group\}` |  | `{group}` after an edge's id: the edge meets the border of the id's group, not the id. |
| INITIAL | ARROW_INTO | `[<>]` |  | `<` or `>` next to `--`: an arrowhead at that end (`a:R --> L:b`; either character works on either end). |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the diagram's title, the rest of the line (kept, not drawn). |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | A text icon: `"…"` or `'…'` after a service's id, drawn as text in place of an icon; `\` escapes the next character, and it may span lines. |
| INITIAL | ID | `\w(?:[-\w]*\w)?` |  | An id: ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`, not ending in `-`. Services, junctions and groups share one set of ids. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\r?\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | ICON | `\([-\w:]+\)` |  | `(database)`: an icon, a built-in name (`cloud`, `database`, `disk`, `internet`, `server`) or a pack's `prefix:name`. |
| INITIAL | LABEL | `\[(?:"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'\|[^\[\]\r\n]+)\]` |  | `[Label]` or `["Label"]`: a label. Unquoted, it holds no bracket or line break; quoted, it may hold both, and `\"` or `\'` is the quote. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
